visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video starts with a wide shot at New Chitose Airport featuring a massive white, red, and black "HOKKAIDO LOVE!" sign. In the background, the modern architectural glass and metal frames of the terminal are visible under bright, even indoor lighting. (2) A person's hand enters the frame, prominently holding a white rectangular box of "De Hokkaido Butter cheese sand Petit". The box features colorful illustrations of a red-roofed barn, green pastures, and grazing cows, conveying a rustic, dairy-focused theme. (3) The camera moves to a close-up of a retail display shelf stacked high with numerous boxes of the product. A price tag in the foreground clearly displays "2,700" yen, surrounded by other identical white boxes in a clean, organized shopping environment. (4) A hand reaches out to pick up a smaller version of the snack box from a dense stack. The bright studio-like lighting of the shop reflects off the smooth white cardboard packaging, emphasizing the abundance of the product available for purchase. (5) The scene transitions to a hand holding a single, individually wrapped snack piece. The wrapper is a distinctive light pink color and is folded into a precise hexagonal shape, presented against a blurred, bright background that suggests a home or cafe setting. (6) The individual wrapper is carefully opened by hand to reveal a round, golden-brown sandwich cookie nestled in a small paper cup. A clear plastic protective ring is seen around the edges of the biscuit layers to prevent breakage during transport. (7) A close-up shot focuses on the sandwich cookie, which consists of three layers of crisp biscuit and two thick layers of smooth white cream. The cross-section after a bite shows the rich, dense texture of the filling and the crumbly nature of the biscuit. (8) The video ends with a full-screen pink graphic overlay. It features the "Japanuts" logo, a website URL, and social media icons for Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube, encouraging viewers to follow for more information on Japanese travel and food.
